title: Nearly quadratic bit complexity for perfectly secure asynchronous Byzantine agreement
formal: Is there a randomized asynchronous binary Byzantine-agreement protocol tolerating every t<n/3 with perfect security and expected Õ(n²) communication bits, using private authenticated channels and no setup?
definitions: There are n processes with binary inputs and reliable asynchronous point-to-point channels. Byzantine processes may deviate arbitrarily; honest processes must agree, and if all honest inputs equal b then their decision must be b. Perfect security requires zero probability of a safety violation against computationally unbounded adversaries, with almost-sure termination under fair delivery. Communication is to be measured for honest processes; faulty processes cannot be charged a bounded number of arbitrary transmissions.

context_blocks.text: Byzantine agreement is a basic fault-tolerance primitive. Nearly quadratic communication with optimal resilience and information-theoretic security would combine the strongest correctness guarantee with a fundamental efficiency scale.

ABEL obtains efficient multivalue extension given a binary agreement primitive. Its extension overhead is not a complete binary protocol with that communication bound. The candidate keeps the underlying binary agreement question separate from the solved extension result.

why: Close a basic communication gap for agreement without computational trust assumptions.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
